sources.title: Laurel: a Re-evaluation of the Spatial, Social and Temporal Paradigms
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of radiocarbon dates, ceramic seriation, regional composites, expansion, contraction, houses, and community patterning.

sources.title: Seymourville Lagoon Upgrade heritage assessment
sources.note: Manitoba government registry report placing Laurel broadly around 200 BCE to 1000 CE.

sources.title: The Woodland Tradition in Minnesota
sources.note: State archaeological synthesis of Laurel phases, wild rice, mounds, artifacts, skeletal evidence, and research limitations.

sources.title: Wanipigow Lake Archaeological Site
sources.note: Manitoba provincial heritage record for early pottery, fish, small mammals, waterfowl, wild rice, and goosefoot.

sources.title: Keeyask Transmission Project Heritage Technical Report
sources.note: Government technical account of Laurel chronology, coil and paddle-and-anvil pottery, decoration, tools, and preservation bias.

sources.title: Lake Winnipeg East System Heritage Resources Technical Report
sources.note: Government comparison of Laurel ceramics with neighboring wares and gradual, regionally uneven Terminal Woodland change.

sources.title: Cultural Heritage Resources Technical Supporting Document
sources.note: Federal assessment evidence for Heron Bay bone tools, copper distribution, trade materials, and organic preservation limits.

sources.title: History and Culture at Kay-Nah-Chi-Wah-Nung
sources.note: Rainy River First Nations site interpretation of recurring use, Laurel mounds, gatherings, fishing, and sacred landscape.

sources.title: State of Protected Heritage Areas: Manitou Mounds
sources.note: Federal heritage report describing Rainy River shoreline, habitation areas, burial mounds, partnership, and site protection.

sources.title: Grand Mound Historic Site
sources.note: Minnesota Historical Society account of spring fishing, seasonal villages, sacred mounds, consultation, closure, and descendant uncertainty.

sources.title: The Armstrong Mound on Rainy River, Ontario
sources.note: Parks Canada archaeological report on basket-loaded earth, collective and child burials, village debris, pottery, and dating limits.

sources.title: Punctured Human Bones of the Laurel Culture from Smith Mound Four
sources.note: Peer-reviewed analysis of an approximately 565 CE mound, modified remains, inherited affiliation hypothesis, and alternative interpretations.

sources.title: An Analysis of Laurel House Structures in Northwestern Ontario
sources.note: University thesis on Laurel chronology, seasonal mobility, house evidence, family inferences, and the rarity of excavated structures.

sources.title: Job (FeJp-3): Tracing Laurel Lifeways in Northern Ontario
sources.note: McMaster archaeological repository record for a 600 to 1200 CE campsite, lithics, mobility, and northern land use.

sources.title: The Potential of Microfossil Use in Paleodiet and Paleoenvironmental Analysis
sources.note: University thesis using pottery residues and phytoliths to test wild rice and maize consumption with explicit sample-bias limits.

sources.title: Food Residue Analysis in the Upper Midwest
sources.note: University thesis defining dated residue samples and evidence limits for Laurel and Brainerd food processing.

sources.title: Laurel in Northern Manitoba: A Ceramic Synthesis
sources.note: Canadian Archaeological Association synthesis of regional pottery, decorative variation, and unusually late thermoluminescence dates.

sources.title: The River House Complex: Middle Woodland on the Northwestern Periphery
sources.note: Peer-reviewed regional taxonomy separating related Saskatchewan assemblages from Laurel and dating open-water occupations.

sources.title: Initial Shield Woodland tradition summary
sources.note: Yale archaeological synthesis of settlement, subsistence, regional interaction, mounds, skeletal scarcity, and identity uncertainty.

sources.title: Cultural Resources Survey of Pukaskwa National Park
sources.note: Parks Canada archaeological synthesis of Laurel mounds, bone tools, copper, exchange goods, and organic preservation limits.

sources.title: The Laurel Culture in Minnesota
sources.note: Yale-indexed monograph warning that Laurel and Blackduck mound assemblages can be mixed and affiliations unclear.

sources.title: Campus Lake Conservation Reserve Management Statement
sources.note: Ontario government account of pottery as an archaeological discriminator, water routes, trade, and sparse interior use.

sources.title: People and Places: A Human History of the Apostle Islands
sources.note: National Park Service synthesis of regional absences, preservation, and later Blackduck overlap around Lake Superior.

sources.title: Statewide Survey of Historical and Archaeological Sites
sources.note: Minnesota public archaeology project describing regional Woodland ceramics, mound burial, wild rice, survey, and preservation.

sources.title: Indigenous Archaeology in Ontario
sources.note: Ontario guidance on Indigenous sites, everyday artifacts, funerary materials, dignity, and community engagement.

sources.title: Zooarchaeology in the South Central Canadian Shield
sources.note: University study of faunal evidence, preservation, fishing, hunting, seasonality, and mixed archaeological deposits.

sources.title: Residue Analysis of Pre-contact Small and Miniature Pottery
sources.note: University research testing practice-pot, toy, cup, bowl, mortuary, and child-associated interpretations through residue analysis.

sources.title: Lake Manitoba and Lake St. Martin Outlet Heritage Resources Report
sources.note: Government report on Initial Woodland chronology, Laurel in boreal settings, wild rice, trade, and Blackduck overlap.
